original_title: Non‐symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine‐Containing Peptides Promoted by Intramolecular Non‐Covalent Interactions
title: Stapling two different tyrosines without crosslinking everything else
blurb: Ethenesulfonyl fluoride anchors covalently to one tyrosine, held in place first by a noncovalent interaction, and then staples it to a second, distinct tyrosine elsewhere in the peptide. The whole point is getting that site-selectivity without the usual intermolecular crosslinking mess nonsymmetric stapling tends to produce.

original_title: Covalent Labeling of Human Neuroglobin with a 19F-Probe to Study its Conformational Changes Using 19F NMR
title: A fluorine tag for watching neuroglobin flex
blurb: A Ph-OCF3 probe gets hung off Cys120 of human neuroglobin, with extra cysteines placed via a C120S background, then read out by 19F NMR. It catches the conformational shift when the Cys46-Cys55 disulfide breaks and again when the protein binds cytochrome c, a decent way to watch a small redox switch move without needing a crystal of every state.

original_title: Novel Covalent FAP-Targeted Radiotherapy Drug Based on DOTA-FAP-2286 for Enhanced Tumor Uptake, Retention, and Therapeutic Efficacy.
title: A covalent anchor for FAP-targeted radiotherapy
blurb: A covalent version of DOTA-FAP-2286 built to improve on the standard noncovalent construct's tumor uptake, retention, and efficacy. Pitched as better, no comparative numbers here to check that against.

original_title: Operational reliability of an automated(176)Lu-based daily quality control system: a five-month continuous monitoring study in digital PET/CT.
title: Does the Lu-176 QC robot actually hold up?
blurb: Five months of continuous monitoring on an automated Lu-176-based daily quality control system for digital PET/CT, essentially an audit of the machine that checks the machine. Useful if you're the one who has to trust it every morning.

original_title: Preparation artefacts mask the detectability of crosslinking-induced structural changes in electron microscopy of collagen hydrogels.
title: Your collagen EM prep might be hiding the crosslinking changes, not showing them
blurb: Standard sample-prep artefacts mask the structural changes that crosslinking is supposed to produce in collagen hydrogels under electron microscopy. Worth a second look at any EM-based crosslinking claim that didn't control for this.

original_title: Primary standardization and <math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" altimg="si20.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1360" class="math"><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray emission intensity determination <math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" altimg="si18.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1365" cl
title: Recalibrating a radionuclide's decay numbers, the unglamorous way
blurb: Primary standardization and gamma-emission-intensity measurements for a radionuclide, the dull metrology work that every downstream activity measurement quietly leans on.

original_title: Progression After PRRT Is Not Just RECIST: Rethinking the Role of SSTR PET
title: RECIST might not know when PRRT actually stops working
blurb: The argument: RECIST-based progression calls miss what's actually happening after PRRT, and SSTR PET deserves more say in deciding when the treatment has failed. A JNM perspective piece, so it's making a case rather than reporting new data.

original_title: One-Pot Hierarchical Assembly of Simple Molecules to Vinylene- and Indole-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
title: One cheap nitrile, two different COF linkages
blurb: The usual COF bottleneck is that the simple, unsymmetric, cheap building blocks don't assemble into anything ordered. Here one such molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile, gets pushed through orthogonal reactivity in a single pot to give both vinylene-linked and indole-linked frameworks. Same cheap starting material, two linkage chemistries, which is the actual trick.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Gold-Catalyzed Chemoselective Dearomative Ring-Opening Modes of Indoles
title: Gold catalyst rips an indole open instead of just dearomatizing it
blurb: Gold plus a Lewis or Brønsted acid pushes ynone-nitriles onto indoles, and instead of the usual dearomatization you get the ring snapping open via an iminyl attack on the indoleninium's C2. Route to 4-azafluorenones, and switching the catalyst and acid flips the reaction between 1+1 and 2+1 component modes. Mechanistically fun even if azafluorenones aren't a huge market.

original_title: Process Development of a Key Chiral Intermediate toward the Synthesis of ABBV-576
title: Swapping a cryogenic step for an enzyme to make ABBV-576's key piece
blurb: The original route to this cystic fibrosis candidate's chiral intermediate needed cryo conditions and still gave mediocre chiral purity. The fix is a ketoreductase-catalyzed dynamic kinetic resolution instead, fed by an epoxidation/Meinwald-rearrangement route to the starting material, which gets both selectivity and purity up without the deep freeze. Unglamorous but exactly the kind of process chemistry that decides whether a drug is actually manufacturable.

original_title: First-In-Human PET Imaging of Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A with [18F]BIBD-181: Automation, Biodistribution, Dosimetry, and Preliminary Application in Epilepsy.
title: SV2A finally gets a first-in-human PET tracer
blurb: [18F]BIBD-181 goes from automated radiosynthesis straight to humans here, with biodistribution and dosimetry worked out and an early look at epilepsy imaging. Early days for the tracer, but SV2A imaging has been mostly riding on a couple of older ligands, so another validated option matters.

original_title: Chemical Synthesis of a Copepod-Derived Artificial Luciferase and Characterization of Site-specific Oxidation During Bioluminescence
title: Building a copepod luciferase from scratch to watch it oxidize
blurb: Copepod luciferases are structurally murky despite being bioimaging workhorses, so they chemically synthesized picALuc, a minimal artificial version, to get a homogeneous sample instead of whatever heterogeneity you'd get biologically. That let them pin down site-specific oxidation during the actual bioluminescent reaction. A mechanism paper dressed up as a synthesis paper.

original_title: A Constant-Current Electrochemical Microreactor-Mass Spectrometry Platform: In Situ Intermediate Capture and Reaction Prediction for C−N Coupling
title: An EC-MS rig built for the constant-current world industry actually uses
blurb: Nearly all electrochemistry-mass spec mechanism work runs potentiostatic, but industrial electrosynthesis runs galvanostatic, so the mechanistic literature has been studying a mode nobody scales up. This microreactor-MS platform runs constant-current instead and catches intermediates in situ, demonstrated on C-N coupling among other reactions. Closes a gap that's been sitting there for a while.

original_title: Formal [3 + 1 + 2] Cyclization/Cyclopropanation Cascade: A Modular Approach to Cyclopropane-Fused Dihydro-α-carbolines
title: Four bonds, two rings, one cascade, to carbolines nobody had an easy route to
blurb: A cascade of C-N coupling, double Michael addition, intramolecular cyclopropanation and sulfonyl elimination builds cyclopropane-fused dihydro-α-carbolines in one go, with decent substrate scope. The payoff: acid treatment opens the cyclopropane back up into indole-fused seven-membered azacycles, so the strained product is really a detour to a different ring system.

original_title: Simultaneous determination of osimertinib and almonertinib concentrations in human plasma and cerebrospinal fluid using UPLC-MS/MS method and its clinical applications
title: Telling two EGFR inhibitors apart in spinal fluid, not just blood
blurb: A UPLC-MS/MS method that measures osimertinib and almonertinib simultaneously in both plasma and CSF, aimed at NSCLC patients with brain metastases. The point isn't the assay itself, it's using it to actually check how well each drug crosses into the CNS and whether that tracks with how patients do clinically.

original_title: HFIP-Promoted Bis-Phosphorylation via Dual C–P Coupling of Unprotected sec -Propargylic Alcohols and Phosphites: Access to Substituted (Prop-2-ene-1,2-diyl)( E )-Bisphosphonates
title: HFIP turns propargyl alcohols into bisphosphonates with no metal and no protecting groups
blurb: Unprotected secondary propargylic alcohols couple straight with phosphites in HFIP, no transition metal, forming both C(sp2)-P and C(sp3)-P bonds at once to give substituted bisphosphonates. Runs at room temperature, scales to grams, and they distill the HFIP back out to reuse it, so the green chemistry pitch is at least partly earned.

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
title: A Wacker oxidation that shrinks the ring instead of just oxidizing it
blurb: Normal Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes would stop at beta-hydride elimination, but here the oxypalladation intermediate takes a semipinacol rearrangement detour instead, contracting the ring to give cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones across 31 examples up to 91% yield. Pre-coordinating the palladium even gets you stereoselective all-syn cyclopropanes. A side door into a ring system people normally reach through dedicated cyclopropanation.

original_title: Hypervalent Iodine Phenol Dearomatization Mediated by Mechanochemistry
title: Ball milling takes over phenol dearomatization from toxic solvents
blurb: Hypervalent iodine(III) reagents turn a cheap aromatic into a functionalized dienone in one step, a quick way to build complexity toward natural products and drugs. The usual catch is needing perfluorinated alcohols as solvent, which wrecks the green metrics. This swaps that out for a ball mill instead.

original_title: Inhibitory Effects of Metal Ions in Radiopharmaceuticals on PCR Amplification for Rapid Sterility Tests.
title: Metal ions in radiopharmaceuticals mess with PCR sterility tests
blurb: PCR-based sterility testing is supposed to be the fast alternative to old-school culture tests, but metal ions sitting in the radiopharmaceutical formulation apparently inhibit the amplification itself, which undercuts the whole point of a rapid test.

original_title: Advances in stability-indicating RP-HPLC for flavonoid analysis: transitioning from conventional to green analytical approaches
title: Stability-indicating RP-HPLC for flavonoids, greened up
blurb: A look at pushing flavonoid stability testing by RP-HPLC away from the conventional toxic solvents and mobile phases toward greener analytical methods.
venue: Journal of Inclusion Phenomena and Macrocyclic Chemistry

original_title: Radioligand Therapy in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer and the LUNAR Trial - Amar Kishan - UroToday
title: A urologist's take on radioligand therapy for oligometastatic prostate cancer
blurb: Commentary tying radioligand therapy use in oligometastatic prostate cancer to the LUNAR trial.

original_title: An RI-NMR and DFT Study of Boron Homologations: Structures of α-Halo Lithium Carbenoids and the Effect of Boronic Ester Structure on 1,2-Metalate Rearrangement Rates
title: Catching lithium carbenoids before they rearrange
blurb: Rapid-injection NMR at -105°C pins down the structure of alpha-halo lithium carbenoids used in boron homologations: 13C-6Li coupling confirms direct C-Li bonding, and DOSY shows they're monomeric, THF-solvated species rather than aggregates. They then trapped the alpha-bromo carbenoid with different arylboronic esters to clock how the boronic ester's structure changes the 1,2-metalate rearrangement rate.

original_title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
title: Wiring an electrode to a radical's lifetime to aminate methane
blurb: Selective methane functionalization at ambient conditions is the usual holy grail, blocked both by the inert C-H bond and by reactive intermediates that die before they can be put to use. This couples radical generation to in situ interfacial interception at an electrode, timing the radical's short life to the electrochemical step so amination happens instead of decay.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Oxidant‐Free Mechanochemical N‐Arylation of Sulfoximines Using Zero‐Valent Copper Powder and Arylboronic Acid
title: Ball-milled copper swaps out the oxidant for N-arylating sulfoximines
blurb: Modifying sulfoximines for drug chemistry usually means noble metals, toxic solvents, or an external oxidant. This does the C-N coupling with plain zero-valent copper powder and arylboronic acid under ball milling, no oxidant needed, and claims it works across a broad range of substrates.

original_title: Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
title: A method that reads cell state changes as causal chains, not snapshots
blurb: CauTrigger treats a biological state transition as a layered causal cascade rather than a bag of isolated molecular changes, which is meant to separate real causal signal from spurious variation in omics data. It also flags likely upstream triggers and predicts how perturbing them would play out, turning raw measurements into testable mechanistic hypotheses.

original_title: Immobilization of a Carboxylated Iridium(III) Complex on NH2-UiO-66: A Robust MOF-Based Photosensitizer for Photodynamic Therapy
title: An iridium photosensitizer bolted onto a zirconium MOF for PDT
blurb: Type II photodynamic therapy needs oxygen, which tumors are stingy with. This nanocomposite conjugates a carboxylated iridium(III) complex onto amino-functionalized UiO-66 via amidation, and TEM, SEM, IR, XPS and elemental mapping confirm it's built as intended. That's proof the material holds together, not proof it beats hypoxia in an actual tumor.

original_title: Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed Divergent Functionalization of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes
title: Germanium light catalysis picks the pyridyl halide out of a crowd
blurb: A photoinduced Ge(II) catalyst forms an electron donor-acceptor complex in situ to generate pyridyl radicals with no added photocatalyst, under mild protic conditions, then couples them to aryl, alkynyl, or alkenyl partners. It's selective enough to hit the pyridyl C-X bond and leave other aryl halides alone, even electron-poor ones, and it opens up C8-selective transformations too.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Möbius Aromatic Figure-Eight Knotted Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
title: A figure-eight knot that's aromatic, and they built a framework out of it
blurb: Möbius aromaticity is a topological twist on aromaticity that's hard to pin down in a real molecule, let alone a polymer network. They made a knotted figure-eight macrocycle (HTE) that's Möbius aromatic, alongside a related ring (TTE) that's antiaromatic, then wove the aromatic one into an extended 3D covalent organic framework. Getting that kind of topological control into an infinite network, not just a single molecule, is the actual feat.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: MS-Based Proteomics Approach in Mapping Protein-Protein Interaction.
title: Mass spec's standard toolkit for mapping protein interactions
blurb: A review chapter walking through how MS-based proteomics gets used to map protein-protein interactions. No new data, just a survey of the methods.

original_title: Automated DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis on Magnetic Anion Exchange Resin
title: Finally automating the one manual step left in DNA-encoded library synthesis
blurb: Split-and-pool DEL synthesis has stayed stubbornly manual while the rest of the workflow got automated around it. This swaps in a magnetic anion-exchange resin, run on a KingFisher Apex, that adsorbs the DNA conjugates and excludes over 95% of unused oligos at the low-salt step, then runs the on-DNA chemistry right on that resin-bound "WAX-ON" substrate. Unglamorous plumbing fix, but exactly the kind DEL chemists have been waiting for.

original_title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
title: An open framework for deep visual proteomics anyone can run
blurb: OpenDVP packages the experimental and computational pipeline for deep visual proteomics so other labs can actually use it, aiming for scalable, high-resolution proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods instead of one lab's bespoke setup.

original_title: A Molecular Switch with Dual Responses to Electrochemical and Mechanical Stimuli
title: A single-molecule switch that answers to both voltage and force
blurb: Most molecular switches take one kind of input; this BODIPY-based junction takes two orthogonal ones, electrochemical and mechanical. Push the gate voltage past -0.6 V and the BODIPY core drops to a stable radical anion that functions as a logic state, so the two stimuli are actually doing distinct, addressable jobs rather than just both happening to flip the same switch.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Iodine-Catalyzed Coupling of α-Bromoketone-Derived Bunte Salts with β-Enaminonitriles: Access to Thiazole-5-carbonitriles via In Situ Thiazine Formation and Skeletal Editing
title: Building thiazoles by editing a thiazine mid-reaction
blurb: An iodine-catalyzed coupling aimed at making 1,4-thiazines instead landed on 2,4-diarylthiazole-5-carbonitriles, with the thiazine apparently forming first and then getting edited down to the thiazole. X-ray confirms the product, and it comes together from readily available starting materials, which is the real selling point for a route that started out chasing something else entirely.

original_title: Extending the Stretchability Limit of Elastomers Through Mechanical Bond Motion
title: Elastomers that dodge the stiffness-versus-stretch trade-off with a rotaxane crosslinker
blurb: Crank up crosslink density in a normal elastomer and you buy stiffness at the cost of stretch. A [2]rotaxane crosslinker sidesteps that: the mechanical bond carries hidden extra length that only unspools under load, redistributing stress through the network instead of letting one weak point snap first. Pitched at soft robotics and implantable bioelectronics, applications that live or die on exactly this kind of durability under repeated strain.

original_title: When Organic Chemistry Meets Surface Science: From Nanographene Characterization to Single-Molecule Reactions
title: What surface science can do that solution-phase chemistry can't
blurb: A review on using scanning probe microscopy and on-surface synthesis to build and interrogate nanographenes and other reactive carbon nanostructures atom by atom, including reactions that simply don't run in a flask. More a field survey than a single result, but a useful map of where that boundary currently sits.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dual‐Electrode Catalytic Engineering for Sustainable C─C Bond Construction via Paired Electrochemical α‐Alkylation of Nitriles
title: Syncing both electrodes so a paired electrolysis actually behaves
blurb: Paired electrolyses tend to fall apart because the anode churns out intermediates faster than the cathode can use them, so you get buildup and side reactions. Here an Fe-doped NiO anode and a Pb/C cathode are tuned together to keep alcohol oxidation and nitrile alpha-alkylation in step, using alcohols as the alkyl source instead of the usual halide reagents. The interfacial matching between the two electrodes is the actual contribution, not just the swap to electrochemistry.

original_title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO<sub>2</sub> electrolysis
title: Water is the gatekeeper for CO2 at the electrode surface
blurb: Using 2D correlated operando Raman plus ab initio molecular dynamics, this traces how water structure at the electrode-electrolyte interface controls how much CO2 can even reach the surface, and that access, not just the catalyst itself, shapes product selectivity at the high current densities that would matter outside a lab. Mechanistic insight rather than a new catalyst, but the kind of detail that's been missing from CO2 electrolysis under realistic conditions.

original_title: Fibronectin Tethering as a Shear-thinning Bio-Annealing Strategy for Granular Hydrogels
title: Gluing hydrogel microparticles together with fibronectin instead of glue chemistry
blurb: Granular hydrogel scaffolds usually get their mechanical stability from annealing adjacent microparticles with photopolymerized crosslinks or guest-host chemistry. Here fibronectin tethering itself does the shear-thinning bio-annealing, so the ECM protein pulls double duty as structural glue rather than just a cell-adhesion afterthought.

original_title: Enhancements and reference internal dosimetry data for the MOBY whole-body computational phantom of the laboratory mouse.
title: An upgrade to the standard mouse you irradiate in software
blurb: Enhancements to the MOBY computational mouse phantom plus a fresh set of reference internal dosimetry values, the unglamorous infrastructure update that every preclinical dose calculation downstream quietly depends on.

original_title: Asymmetric Metathesis Dimerization/Desymmetrization of C s ‐Symmetric Divinylferrocenes: Enantioselective Deactivation of Vinyl Groups and Subsequent Kinetic Resolution of Chiral Dimers
title: Getting a molybdenum catalyst to pick sides between two identical vinyl groups
blurb: A chiral Mo-alkylidene catalyst, paired with either enantiomer of a binaphtholate ligand, tells apart the two enantiotopic vinyl groups on Cs-symmetric divinylferrocenes well enough to dimerize one selectively while leaving the other alone. Then it kinetically resolves the resulting chiral dimers in the same system, so desymmetrization and resolution both fall out of one metathesis setup.

original_title: Photocatalytic Formal [4 + 2] Radical Annulation of α-Bromoacetylindoles with Alkenes: Broad Scope and Synthesis of (±)-Goniomitine
title: A blue-light [4+2] that builds the goniomitine core on the way
blurb: A ruthenium-photocatalyzed radical annulation stitches α-bromoacetylindoles onto both electron-rich and electron-poor alkenes, giving 30 dihydropyrido[1,2-a]indolone derivatives in up to 88% yield. The scope is broad enough that they cap it off with a short synthesis of (±)-goniomitine rather than stopping at the methodology.

original_title: Transition-metal-catalyzed regioselective CN bond formation of benzotriazoles
title: Finally getting benzotriazoles to react on the N2 side
blurb: A review tracking how transition-metal catalysis, with help from a few Lewis acids, has chipped away since 2009 at a stubborn selectivity problem: classical electrophilic chemistry on benzotriazoles defaults to the N1 product, leaving the more useful N2-functionalized isomer the hard one to reach.

original_title: Comparison of 99mTc-Phytate and 99mTc-Antimony Trisulfide in sentinel lymph node detection: a lymphoscintigraphy study in breast cancer patients.
title: Two old Tc-99m colloids, head to head for finding the sentinel node
blurb: A lymphoscintigraphy comparison of 99mTc-phytate against 99mTc-antimony trisulfide for sentinel lymph node detection in breast cancer patients. Not a new tracer, just the kind of practical bake-off that decides what a department actually stocks.

original_title: Simultaneous quantification of duloxetine and 1-naphthol in pharmaceutical and biological matrices using a sensitive and eco-friendly synchronous fluorescence technique
title: Telling duloxetine from its genotoxic impurity when their fluorescence spectra are twins
blurb: Duloxetine and the genotoxic process impurity 1-naphthol fluoresce almost identically, which breaks ordinary fluorometric QC. A synchronous fluorescence method separates them anyway, and it's pitched as the greener option too.
venue: Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences

original_title: ON/OFF Photoswitching of Magnetism and Luminescence in a Compact Bis(Nitronylnitroxyl)Dithienylethene Diradical
title: A biradical switch chemists apparently couldn't make until now
blurb: A compact bis(nitronylnitroxide) dithienylethene diradical that computations flagged as magnetically promising years ago but that evidently took this long to actually synthesize. Hitting it with 365 nm light isomerizes the switch and flips both its magnetism and a near-IR emission (720-840 nm) localized on the radical, two properties off one photochemical trigger.

original_title: Photoinduced Consecutive Ferrous‐ and Ferric‐Catalyzed Single‐Electron Transfers
title: Iron photoredox running its ferrous and ferric tricks back to back, no extra oxidant needed
blurb: Iron photoredox papers usually commit to one lane, either ferric LMCT or ferrous electron transfer, each leaning on an added oxidant or reductant to close the cycle. This one lets the ferrous and ferric species interconvert in situ, running a redox-neutral consecutive LMCT/ET sequence that does 1,2-dialkylation of alkenes without feeding in outside redox reagents.

original_title: Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO<sub>2</sub> electroreduction
title: Using a magnetic field to cook carbonate off the CO2 reduction catalyst
blurb: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode from local alkalinity is a standing durability problem in CO2 electroreduction. An alternating magnetic field heats a ferromagnetic high-entropy alloy catalyst from the inside, which suppresses that carbonate buildup and stretches operating life in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes.

original_title: Durable, highly loaded atomically dispersed catalysts via a reticular coordination strategy
title: Pinning single Pt atoms so they stop wandering off
blurb: Coordinate one Pt atom to each Ce-oxo cluster in a MOF, calcine it, and you get ceria loaded with 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt that resists sintering even under harsh reducing conditions. Normally cramming that much single-atom metal onto a support just gets you clumps; the lattice confinement is doing the actual work here.

original_title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
title: Getting electrolyte to actually wet a MOF catalyst
blurb: Covalent MOFs are structurally precise but usually sit there poorly wetted and electrochemically dead for making H2O2 via the two-electron oxygen reduction route. The fix here is dosing in cationic groups to modulate interfacial charge, turning the framework into a surface the electrolyte actually reaches. Pitched as a greener alternative to the anthraquinone process, though the cut-off snippet means no real numbers yet.

original_title: Surrounded Catalysts Prepared by Ion Exchange Inverse Loading: Design Strategies, Structural Features, and Catalytic Applications
title: Building the support around the catalyst instead of the other way round
blurb: A review on ion-exchange inverse loading, where you grow the support around the active metal rather than dropping metal onto a premade support. The resulting "surrounded catalysts" get interfacial structures built to resist the sintering and coking that kill ordinary supported catalysts under harsh conditions. It's a survey piece, so no new data, just a map of what's been built this way.

original_title: Impact of Ether Side‐Chain Length and Anion Structure on the Physicochemical and Electrochemical Properties of Tetrahydrothiophenium Ionic Liquids
title: Tuning ionic liquids by how many oxygens you cram into the side chain
blurb: A series of tetrahydrothiophenium ionic liquids with ether side chains of one to four oxygens, run against FSA or TFSA anions. Longer ether chains push the glass transition temperature up, and whether the stuff crystallizes or just glasses over depends on chain length, anion choice, and cooling rate. Useful knobs for dialing in a specific liquid range, less a result than a map of the design space.

original_title: Complementary Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
title: Turning acetonitrile into the ethyl group on your amine
blurb: Mixed Cu-Ni oxide electrodes couple acetonitrile reduction with benzylamine right at the electrolyte interface, and the best version, Cu-NiO-0.5, delivers N-ethylbenzylamine in 75% yield at 87% selectivity at -0.5 V. A one-pot electrochemical route to N-ethylamines that normally need separate reduction and amination steps.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sulfur-Coordinated Iron Overcomes Stability Limitations in Atomically Dispersed Metal-Nitrogen-Carbon Catalysts for CO 2 Electrolysis
title: Swapping nitrogen for sulfur to keep the iron sites from dying
blurb: Fe-N-C catalysts for CO2 reduction look fine until you push industrial current densities, where the Fe sites degrade fast. Here they deliberately coordinate sulfur around the iron instead, building Fe-S5-type sites into a dual-metal Fe-Sy/Ni-Nx-C catalyst, and that swap is what buys back the durability.

original_title: Polyoxometalate-modified AgAu nanoalloy electrocatalysts for highly efficient nitrate-to-ammonia conversion
title: Getting nitrate-to-ammonia to work without cranking the pH
blurb: Nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction usually struggles in near-neutral water because the multi-proton-coupled electron transfer drags, which matters if you want this to run on actual wastewater instead of a strongly basic lab solution. The fix is a polyoxometalate-modified AgAu nanoalloy meant to speed that step up. The snippet stops short of giving efficiency numbers, but the framing of nitrate cleanup and ammonia recovery as one process is the point.

original_title: Copper‐Catalyzed Mechanochemical Racemization of BINOL
title: Ball-milling your way to racemizing BINOL
blurb: Racemizing enantiopure BINOL normally means a solvent-heavy solution reaction, but a CuCl/N-donor ligand system under ball milling does it with 30-fold less solvent. Most of the gain comes from grinding conditions: weakly coordinating aprotic liquid-assisted grinding agents work best, with DCM on top, though they note it's swappable. Handy if you'd rather recycle the wrong enantiomer than toss it.

original_title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
title: Finally separating 'the catalyst is dissolving' from 'the catalyst is working'
blurb: High-entropy oxide OER catalysts dissolve and evolve oxygen at the same time, which makes it hard to know which process you're actually measuring. Pairing AFM with scanning electrochemical cell microscopy on atomically flat, single-faceted perovskite surfaces lets them watch lattice dissolution and water oxidation separately under the same conditions. A methods paper rather than a new catalyst, but exactly the tool this subfield was missing.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Studies on Nickel‐Catalyzed Photo‐Reduction Reaction of Propargylic Derivatives
title: Getting allenes to form where you actually want them
blurb: Regioselective allene formation has been the weak point of nickel-catalyzed propargylic coupling, and this nickel-catalyzed photoreduction of propargylic acetates nails it, delivering 1,3-disubstituted and trisubstituted allenes with broad functional group tolerance. They also route the products into alkenyl boronic compounds and 1,3-dienes, with mechanistic work backing up why the selectivity holds.

original_title: PNNH–Ru-Catalyzed Highly E-Selective Semi-Hydrogenation of Alkynes Using MeOH as a Hydrogen Donor
title: Swap the H2 tank for a bottle of methanol
blurb: A new PNNH-Ru complex semi-hydrogenates alkynes to E-alkenes using methanol as the hydrogen source instead of pressurized H2 gas, with high yields and good stereoselectivity under mild conditions. Kinetics point to an active ruthenium dihydride doing the actual work. No high-pressure rig needed, which is most of the appeal.

original_title: Enantioselective Amination of In Situ Generated Alkyl Gold Species with Azocarboxamide as the N -Source
title: Gold and a chiral squaramide team up for a nitrogen stereocenter
blurb: In situ alkylgold species generated from N-propargylamides get aminated by azocarboxamides, with a gold catalyst and a chiral quinine-squaramide working in tandem to set a nitrogen-bearing tertiary stereocenter. Yields and ee's both come out high, and the alkylideneoxazoline products are versatile enough to carry forward into further transformations.

original_title: A Phase 1/2 Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Dosimetry, and Anti-tumor Activity of Ga-68-NGUL / Lu-177-DGUL in Patients With Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC) Refractory to Standard Therapy
title: Another Ga-68/Lu-177 theranostic pair clears a Phase 1/2 in mCRPC
blurb: Cellbion's Ga-68-NGUL/Lu-177-DGUL diagnostic-therapeutic pair just completed a Phase 1/2 in castration-resistant prostate cancer that had already stopped responding to standard therapy, checking safety, dosimetry, and anti-tumor activity. Just confirmation it ran to completion here, no efficacy numbers yet, which is step one for yet another entrant in an increasingly crowded theranostic field.

original_title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
title: Keeping bismuth from turning into a sponge, for 380 hours straight
blurb: Nitrate-to-hydroxylamine electrocatalysis on bismuth normally degrades through what they're naming electrochemical spongification, where the compact metal relaxes into a disconnected porous mess under continuous electrolysis. An asymmetric pulsed current, basically making the electrode breathe unevenly, decouples that failure from long-term durability and keeps the catalyst running for 380 hours. Naming the failure mode might be the most useful part of this.

original_title: Delta-like Ligand 3–Targeted Imaging in Small Cell Lung Cancer
title: Imaging small cell lung cancer through DLL3 instead of biopsying it
blurb: A DLL3-targeted imaging approach for small cell lung cancer, the same target several SCLC therapies already chase. Thin on detail beyond that, but a non-invasive readout of DLL3 status would matter for picking who actually gets those drugs.

original_title: Photoredox α-Alkylation of Phosphonates by Styrenes
title: Ten minutes, no metal, and your phosphonate gets alkylated
blurb: A photoredox protocol alkylates phosphonates with styrenes in 10 minutes using just 0.1 mol% of an organic photocatalyst, no transition metal involved. It also handles double addition of two different styrenes onto one phosphonate, and the whole thing scales to grams, which is more than most photoredox papers bother to show.

original_title: Protic Poly(Diallylammonium Sulfonate)s: Toward Water‐Processable Fluorine‐Free Ionic Materials
title: Fluorine-free ionic polymers that still dissolve in water
blurb: A new family of protic poly(ionic liquid)s made by cyclopolymerizing diallylammonium monomers, pairing two backbones with three fluorine-free sulfonate counter-ions for six cations total, five never reported before. The point is ionic materials that process in water without dragging along the usual fluorinated anions.

original_title: Ionic Liquids: Synthetic Methodology and ApplicationsA Chronological and Sustainability-Focused Review (2019-2026)
title: Seven years of ionic liquids, sorted by how green they got
blurb: A chronological review tracking ionic liquid synthesis and applications from 2019 to 2026, tracing the field's drift toward fourth-generation bio-based, biodegradable, multifunctional ILs from renewable feedstocks. A map of where the field's been pointed rather than new chemistry of its own.

original_title: Synthesis of 2,3-Diamino-2,3-Dideoxy-β- d -Mannosides via Stereoselective Anomeric O -Alkylation of 2 N ,3 N -Imidazolidinone-Protected d -Mannoses
title: A protecting group that doubles as the stereocontrol
blurb: Cesium carbonate drives anomeric O-alkylation of imidazolidinone-protected diaminomannoses with high beta-selectivity, and that same imidazolidinone ring later opens cleanly via LiAlH4 reduction followed by acid-catalyzed aminal cleavage to reveal the free diamine. They carry it through to a trisaccharide containing the diacetamido-dideoxy-mannoside, so the method actually gets used rather than just shown off on its own.

original_title: Highly Polarized 1,4‐Dihydropyrrolo[3,2‐ b ]Pyrroles: From Synthesis to Photophysics and Two‐Photon Induced Polymerization
title: Tuning a pyrrolopyrrole dye core for two-photon polymerization
blurb: A set of quadrupolar, centrosymmetric dyes built on a ladder-type dihydropyrrolopyrrole core, varying only the peripheral electron-withdrawing groups and the degree of planarity. The ketone versions show charge-transfer bands at 500-600 nm but barely emit, while swapping in dicyanovinylidene groups with more pi-extension shifts the photophysics enough to drive two-photon induced polymerization.

original_title: [Advances in Cardiac Sympathetic PET Imaging: Development and Clinical Translation of (18)F-fluproxadine ((18)F-AF78)].
title: A PET tracer for cardiac nerves, moving from bench to clinic
blurb: F-18-AF78 (fluproxadine) is a PET tracer for cardiac sympathetic innervation, essentially chasing the job I-123 MIBG SPECT has held for decades but with PET's resolution and quantification. This is the development-and-translation writeup, not a trial readout, so no efficacy numbers to chew on yet.

original_title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
title: Making a 2D glass instead of letting it crystallize
blurb: On-surface supramolecular assembly usually just rolls downhill to the enthalpy-favored crystal. Here in situ triradicals on Ag(111) get trapped instead in a genuine non-equilibrium 2D glassy state, which is normally the outcome people are trying to avoid. The payoff is tunable elasticity and phase-change behavior you don't get from a tidy lattice.

original_title: Dual-Polyhedral Distortion for Low-Cost Amorphous Halide Electrolytes with Improved Ionic Conductivity
title: Cheaper amorphous halide electrolytes for sodium batteries
blurb: xNaBF4-ZrCl4 mixes made by one-step ball milling, where Zr4+ and B3+ fight over the same coordination sites and that competition is what distorts the polyhedra and keeps the thing amorphous. The point is knocking cost out of the precursor, with the conductivity bump as a side effect of the disorder.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dynamic Interplay of Dissolved Ions and Solid Surfaces Enables Efficient Nonalkaline Biomass Electrooxidation
title: Letting cobalt dissolve and redeposit instead of fighting it
blurb: Transition-metal catalysts for deep electrooxidation, like turning HMF into FDCA, usually die from reconstruction and leaching in acid or neutral media. Here they just lean into it: Co2+ ions and electrodeposited cobalt oxyhydroxide cycle between dissolved and solid states on purpose, with carboxylate anions apparently helping, and that equilibrium is what drives efficient HMF oxidation without alkaline conditions.

original_title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
title: Shrinking the cage around a single Cu atom to force urea, not side products
blurb: Programmable Zn-node gasification carves 1.5-1.8 nm cavities into a ZIF to host atomically dispersed Cu-N4 sites sized to match the kinetics of CO2/NO3- coupling, with a confinement-metric descriptor (9.64) proposed to predict it. They're claiming near-unity selectivity for urea, which is the actual news since selective C-N coupling is usually where this chemistry falls apart.

original_title: Electrosynthesis of p ‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO 2
title: Skipping the Kolbe-Schmitt brute force for p-hydroxybenzoic acid
blurb: The standard route needs anhydrous phenolate, high temperature and pressure, strong base, and metal cations just to get decent selectivity. Iodine-mediated electrosynthesis gets there straight from phenol and CO2 under milder conditions, 61% yield and 90% selectivity. Not huge numbers, but the mediator is the trick worth noting.

original_title: Thermal EDA-Mediated Divergent Synthesis of Acetimidates and Benzochromenes via a One-Pot Three-Component Reaction
title: One EDA complex, two scaffolds, no catalyst required
blurb: BINOLs and aryldiazonium salts react through an EDA radical pathway with MeCN's cyano carbon doubling as the C1 source, and nothing else added: no metal, light, catalyst, or additive. Whether you get an acetimidate or a benzochromene comes down entirely to the phenol's ortho substituent, Ritter side reactions get suppressed, and axial chirality survives the whole process.

original_title: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
title: One synthetic Mo complex covering four different enzyme families
blurb: Molybdopterin enzymes span everything from oxyanion reduction to C-H hydroxylation via Mo(VI)/Mo(IV) cycling, but synthetic mimics usually stall out by comproportionating into dead Mo(V) dimers. This [N2S2]2- Mo(IV)=O complex pulls oxygen atoms from Me2SO, Me3NO, and ClO4-, stand-ins for three separate enzyme families, and gets to catalytic C-H oxidation on top. The versatility is the finding, not any one reaction.

original_title: Water–Organic Interfaces Drive Molecular Evolution from Squalene to Steroids
title: Squalene turns into a steroid with no enzymes, just water droplets
blurb: Cells need two dedicated enzymes and a 2,3-oxidosqualene intermediate to make lanosterol from squalene. Water microdroplets sitting against an immiscible organic solvent apparently do the whole multistep job on their own, the proposed mechanism being an interfacial electric field generating ROS that epoxidizes squalene, then acid-catalyzed ring opening kicks off a cationic cyclization cascade straight to lanosterol, with H218O labeling backing up where the oxygen lands. A decent argument for how this chemistry could've run before enzymes existed.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF GC-MS METHOD FOR THE QUANTIFICATION OF RESIDUAL DIMETHYL SULFATE, DIETHYL SULFATE AND DIISOPROPYL SULFATE CONTENTS IN RIMEGEPANT SULFATE DRUG SUBSTANCE
title: A GC-MS method to hunt genotoxic alkyl sulfates in rimegepant
blurb: Method development and validation, selective-ion-monitoring GC-MS to quantify three potential genotoxic impurities, dimethyl, diethyl, and diisopropyl sulfate, in rimegepant sulfate drug substance. Not glamorous, but it's exactly the impurity-control work that has to exist before a drug substance clears QC.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

original_title: Ruthenium-Catalyzed Site-Selective Direct Deuteration of Azaarenes Using Deuterium Oxide
title: D2O deuterates azaarenes without a directing group
blurb: A ruthenium hydride catalyst at 0.5-1 mol% swaps C-H for C-D straight off D2O in imidazoles, thiazoles, and indoles, no directing group required. They ran it directly on active drug substances too, which is the part that matters if you want deuterated analogs without redesigning the whole synthesis.

original_title: Selective Formation of a 1,2‐Diborane(4) and Alcohol‐Driven B─B Bond Cleavage to Generate H 2
title: Catecholate picks the diborane isomer, then an alcohol cracks it open for H2
blurb: B2Cat2 plus mesityllithium gives the unusual 1,2-disubstituted diborane(4), with the catecholate co-ligand apparently steering which isomer forms. An alcohol then cleaves the B-B bond to release H2, main-group chemistry doing a bond-activation trick usually billed as a transition-metal specialty.

original_title: Sorbitol-nitrate pyrolysis as a method for phase composition control of bismuth oxides and composites based thereon
title: Sorbitol and nitrate burn together to dial in your bismuth oxide polymorph
blurb: Pyrolyzing a sorbitol-nitrate complex, nitrate as oxidizer, sorbitol as reductant, lets you pick alpha, beta, or amorphous Bi2O3, or push further into the beta-Bi2O3/(BiO)2CO3 and alpha/beta-Bi2O3/Bi composites. No fancy equipment needed, which is normally the annoying part of controlling bismuth oxide phase.

original_title: Complete stabilization of surface oxygen vacancies in high-entropy oxides
title: Keeping a high-entropy oxide's surface vacancies from healing themselves
blurb: High-entropy oxides hold onto more oxygen vacancies than simple binary oxides, but the surface ones usually heal over, migrate, or trigger structural collapse once a catalyst actually runs. High-throughput screening of a Cu-Fe-Ni-Cr-Zn oxide claims to stabilize them completely, which would matter a lot for electrocatalysts that currently degrade with use.

original_title: Cooperative Dual-Template Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
title: Two templates fighting it out gets you two pore sizes in one carbon sphere
blurb: Letting Pluronic P123 and L64 cooperate as templates builds mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal, interconnected pores instead of the single periodicity soft-templating usually gives you. The payoff is the pore hierarchy itself boosting charge transport, not just a new way to make spheres.

original_title: Titanium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidation of N -Acylsulfenamides to Chiral N-Acylsulfinamides
title: A titanium catalyst turns sulfenamides chiral without the usual sulfur-oxidation mess
blurb: BINOL/Ti(OiPr)4 with TBHP oxidizes N-acylsulfenamides to chiral N-acylsulfinamides in 56-90% yield and up to 99% ee, across a decent spread of alkyl and heteroaryl groups. Clean asymmetric sulfur oxidation under mild conditions, a reaction class that's usually harder to get stereocontrol out of.

original_title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP
title: DPD and HMDP aren't interchangeable once you look past the heart
blurb: A multicenter retrospective on diagnosing ATTR cardiac amyloidosis finds the two bone tracers differ in whole-body biodistribution, not just cardiac uptake. Extracardiac uptake patterns turn out to carry real diagnostic information, so swapping one tracer for the other isn't the free substitution it's often treated as.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Chemistry of adaptive polymer-based protective coatings for harsh environments: chemical aging, anticorrosion, antifouling, and self-healing design
title: Coatings that do more than just sit there and block water
blurb: A review rounding up polymer coatings built to respond rather than just resist: inhibitor release, antifouling behavior, self-healing, spanning epoxy, polyurethane, siloxane, catechol, zwitterionic, and bio-derived systems for marine, acidic, and humid service. It's a survey, so the value is in the cross-chemistry comparison rather than any single new result.

original_title: Aqueous SEC–MALS Characterization of Hydrophilic Azolium-Based Poly(ionic liquid)s in Their Native Halide Form
title: Getting an honest molar mass out of poly(ionic liquid)s that fight the column
blurb: Imidazolium PILs in their native halide form are a pain for SEC, THF/LiTFSI gives low dn/dc and weak signal, so they screened aqueous mobile phases instead to get usable SEC-MALS data on five hydrophilic PILs. A methods fix for a measurement that's apparently just been unreliable for this polymer class.

original_title: Synthesis of a Crystalline Acylated Lysine Building Block for Retatrutide Manufacture
title: The lysine building block that finally crystallizes, so retatrutide's side chain skips chromatography
blurb: Retatrutide's lipidated side chain is normally a slog to purify, but the new route gets the acylated lysine intermediate to actually crystallize, a rare outcome for lipidated amino acid building blocks, so isolation skips chromatography entirely. That's the kind of process chemistry win that matters once you're making the drug at multi-ton scale, not just making it once.

original_title: Landscape of Endocytic Effectors for Extracellular Targeted Protein Degradation.
title: A field guide to the endocytic machinery degraders actually hijack
blurb: A review mapping out the endocytic effectors that extracellular targeted protein degradation platforms recruit to drag their targets into the cell. No new data, just the landscape sorted into one place.

original_title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts
title: Designing an enzyme to do asymmetric photocatalysis from the ground up
blurb: Artificial metalloenzymes built de novo, not repurposed from an existing protein scaffold, to catalyze enantioselective photoreactions. That's the pitch in Nature; worth a look once the substrate scope and ee numbers show up.

original_title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
title: A coating that sticks to any membrane in minutes, no toxic reagents
blurb: Fenton-catalyzed chemistry lays down a thin cross-linked PVP hydrogel on porous membranes regardless of their chemistry or pore size, done within minutes and without touching the pore architecture. It also holds up against acid and alkali, so this reads like a drop-in retrofit rather than a membrane you'd have to requalify everything around.

original_title: Determination of neutron spectrum for nuclear reactor based on non-extensive statistical theory
title: A non-extensive statistics approach to reactor neutron spectra
blurb: Reformulates neutron spectrum determination for nuclear reactors using non-extensive statistical theory instead of the usual Boltzmann-Gibbs assumptions.

original_title: A Pan-KRAS-Targeted PET Probe for Noninvasive Quantitative Imaging of KRAS Expression
title: One PET probe for all your KRAS mutants
blurb: [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-pKRASi targets KRAS regardless of which mutation is driving the tumor, meant to both identify mutant subtype and quantify expression level without a biopsy. If it holds up clinically it beats genotyping-by-biopsy for picking KRAS-targeted therapy, but a single probe catching every clinically relevant mutant is a big claim to prove.

original_title: Experimentally Derived Microscale Blood and Lymphatic Vasculature Models for Applications to Radiopharmaceutical Dosimetry.
title: Microscale vessel models built for radiopharmaceutical dosimetry math
blurb: Experimentally derived models of blood and lymphatic microvasculature meant to feed radiopharmaceutical dosimetry calculations, a plumbing problem dosimetrists apparently needed better data for.

original_title: [3+2] Cycloaddition of Bicyclic Diaziridines with Acyl Azides: Synthesis of 1,3,5-Triazabicyclo[3.3.0]octanes
title: A catalyst-free route into triazabicyclooctanes
blurb: Bicyclic diaziridines plus acyl azides, no catalyst, straight [3+2] cycloaddition to 1,3,5-triazabicyclo[3.3.0]octane scaffolds. Broad substrate scope including drug- and natural-product-derived motifs, good atom economy, and it scales, so this is a real modular route rather than a one-substrate showcase.

original_title: Beyond Structural Analogy: Electronic and Functional Divergence in Isostructural Zr, Hf, and Th Metal–Organic Frameworks
title: Zr isn't actually a stand-in for Th, electronically speaking
blurb: Build the same M6-ADC framework with Zr, Hf, or Th and you get structurally identical materials, but the Th version has distinct optical and electronic behavior from its Zr and Hf twins. Chemists lean on Zr as the safe nonradioactive surrogate for thorium chemistry; this says the structural match doesn't carry over to the properties that actually matter.

original_title: Inside Back Cover: Thinking Outside the Binding Site: A Self‐Encapsulating Kinase Inhibitor Remodels Its Pocket to Achieve Selectivity
title: A kinase inhibitor that folds up to fit its own pocket
blurb: Cover piece on a kinase inhibitor that remodels the binding pocket around itself, self-encapsulating its way to selectivity instead of just fitting the site as found.

original_title: Mechanoimmuno‐Engineered Dendritic Cell Membrane Nanodiscs Presenting Diverse Antigens for Potent Antibacterial Vaccination
title: Dendritic cell membranes repackaged as an antibacterial vaccine
blurb: Nanodiscs made from dendritic cell membranes, with stiffness tuned on purpose, co-present both bacterial surface antigens and secreted toxins alongside extra immune-stimulatory molecules. The point is finally getting the T-cell response that antibacterial vaccines usually miss by showing the immune system only surface antigens.

original_title: Preclinical evaluation of a CD137-targeted PET tracer for detection of inflammatory arthritis.
title: Imaging arthritis by tracking CD137 instead of just swelling
blurb: A PET tracer aimed at CD137 to flag inflammatory arthritis, tested in animals so far. The pitch is picking up immune activation directly rather than inferring it from joint swelling on an X-ray, but it's preclinical and nobody's pointed this at a human joint yet.

original_title: Anti-HER2 immunotoxin scFv-PE35KDEL internalizes via receptor-mediated endocytosis and induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer cells
title: A pertuzumab-shaped warhead that walks Pseudomonas toxin into ovarian cancer cells
blurb: Anti-HER2 scFv taken from pertuzumab, welded to a trimmed 35 kDa chunk of Pseudomonas exotoxin A with a KDEL tag so the payload gets retained once inside. It binds HER2, gets taken up by receptor-mediated endocytosis, and kills ovarian cancer cells by triggering apoptosis. Still cell-culture work, but the mechanism is clean: hijack the receptor, deliver the toxin, force the cell to kill itself.

original_title: What's holding back droplet microfluidics in everyday lab work?
title: What's holding back droplet microfluidics in everyday lab work?
blurb: Droplet microfluidics sounds promising for screening large numbers of cells or reactions, but it doesn't seem common in every biochemistry lab. Is the main barrier equipment cost, assay setup or trouble adapting existing methods? Would love to hear from anyone whos worked with it.
